findings.description: WH renders introductory 何でも as No matter what instead of a report marker for the teacher's advice.

contexts.japanese: 何でも、ツンツンと残虐を尽くした後に程よくヘタれてデレて見せると、好感度ってヤツが大幅アップするんだろー？
contexts.japanesePC: 何でも、ツンツンと残虐を尽くした後に程よくヘタれてデレて見せると、好感度ってヤツが大幅アップするんだろー？
contexts.japanesePS3: 何でも、ツンツンと残虐を尽くした後に程よくヘタれてデレて見せると、好感度ってヤツが大幅アップするんだろー？
contexts.WH: No matter what, after acting bad-tempered and exploring the depths of cruelty, by acting properly incompetent and soft, you get a massive rise on that goodwill meter thing, ri-ght?
contexts.MG: Apparently, if you start out all hostile and needlessly brutal, then turn incompetent and soft at just the right moment, you can spark a huge bump on your affection meter, ri-ght?
contexts.UP: I hear, after acting {ruby:tsuntsun:bad‐tempered and exploring the depths of cruelty, if you act properly incompetent and {ruby:dere:soft, you can get a massive rise on that goodwill meter thing, riiight?
contexts.note: Full three-witness source-first prose review with context. Canonical parent outcomes independently checked; PC anchors distinguish inherited wording from introduced changes.

findings.sourceReading: Following お師匠様の言う通り, 何でも introduces what she has heard or been told: apparently, showing weakness and affection after cruelty raises favorability.
findings.alternative: 何でも can mean anything in other syntax, but here it introduces the reported explanation and is not the unconditional concessive whatever happens. The closing だろー retains confirmation-seeking tone.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: WH substitutes naive and simple for 天真爛漫 in the narrator's characterization of the formerly laughing Beatrice.

contexts.japanesePC: 彼女を例える言葉は、残虐非道。傍若無人。そして天真爛漫。
contexts.WH: She could be called inhumane and cruel.  Arrogant and outrageous.  And also, naive and simple.
contexts.note: Full three-witness source-first prose review with context. Canonical parent outcomes independently checked; PC anchors distinguish inherited wording from introduced changes.

findings.sourceReading: 天真爛漫 describes unspoiled, spontaneous, openly innocent exuberance, here placed beside cruelty and disregard for others. It does not assert simplicity of intellect or credulity.
findings.alternative: Naive can express innocence and simple can mean unaffected, but together without that qualification they foreground unsophistication while losing exuberant spontaneity; nearby loss of laughter supports the latter trait.
findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. MangaGamer uses the accepted MangaGamer-based Witch Hunt backport, and Umineko Project uses its repository English; both are compared with maintained PS3-derived Japanese. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

contexts.MG: "You can't get the next game ready without waking Beato.
contexts.UP: "You can't get the next game ready without waking Beato.

findings.sourceReading: ベアトを起こせず、あんたに次のゲームを準備も出来ない lists two failures: cannot wake her; cannot prepare the next game either.
findings.alternative: Beatrice supplies previous games, making her absence relevant, but the Japanese does not make waking her the sole prerequisite to Battler preparing one.

findings.description: WH adds brushing hair back where Japanese depicts hair flowing as the woman rises and points.

contexts.japanese: 彼女は立ち上がり、…長い髪をなびかせながら、夏妃伯母さんを指差して、もう一度言った。
contexts.japanesePC: (彼女/・・)は立ち上がり、...長い髪をなびかせながら、夏妃伯母さんを指差して、もう一度言った。
contexts.japanesePS3: 彼女は立ち上がり、…長い髪をなびかせながら、夏妃伯母さんを指差して、もう一度言った。
contexts.WH: She stood up, ...brushed back her long hair, pointed at Natsuhi oba-san and said it one more time.
contexts.MG: She stood up, ...brushed back her long hair, pointed at Aunt Natsuhi, and said it one more time.

findings.sourceReading: 長い髪をなびかせながら means with long hair streaming or fluttering; no hand grooming gesture is specified.
findings.alternative: She could move hair while turning, but brushed back specifies an additional deliberate action and changes the visual sequence.
